assessment_summary: The proof fails because it incorrectly assumes that every nonempty polyhedron has extreme points. In Step 3 (lines 0044-0046), it attempts to construct the polytope X as the convex hull of the extreme points of P. This fails for any polyhedron containing a line (such as P = \mathbb{R}), which has no extreme points, rendering the convex hull empty and breaking the algebraic verification in Step 4 (line 0063). Additionally, the alternative construction in Step 2 contains a blatant algebraic error at line 0040: it deduces Ax - Ac \le b from Ac \le 0, which is backwards since Ac \le 0 implies -Ac \ge 0.
counterexample: Let P = \mathbb{R} (defined by 0x \le 0 in \mathbb{R}^1), which is a nonempty polyhedron. The proof claims in lines 0045-0046 that P can be written as P = conv{v_1, ..., v_k} + cone{r_1, ..., r_l} where v_i are the extreme points of P. However, P = \mathbb{R} has no extreme points (k=0). Consequently, the requirement in Step 4 (line 0063) that \sum_{i=1}^k \lambda_i = 1 cannot be satisfied because an empty sum evaluates to 0. This makes X = conv(\emptyset) = \emptyset, and thus X + C = \emptyset \neq \mathbb{R}.
